methodology: The study involved monitoring yield and mechanical properties of a selected spring flax variety grown both in winter (2022/2023) and in spring (2023). The plants were monitored for four consecutive years, with the winter crop experiencing mild winter conditions favorable for winter crops and a severe spring drought that impacted spring crops.
research_objective: To investigate the feasibility of growing a spring flax variety in winter under varying climatic conditions and to assess the impact on fiber length and lignin content.

key_findings.finding: Cultivating a spring flax variety in winter is feasible under favorable conditions, but the resulting fibers are shorter and more lignified, which may pose technical challenges during spinning.
Winter flax varieties have expanded rapidly in French fields, accounting for over 40% of total textile flax area by 2024.

The Elixirs spring flax was grown for four consecutive years at the same site to assess interannual variability and in 2023 it was cultivated in both spring and winter regimes to allow direct comparison.
Winter cultivation of Elixir Flax variety provides insight into potential adaptation strategy for the flax sector under climate change.
